ai_summary: Great Britain’s power system is currently recording 8.1 GW of total wind output, with estimated Scottish wind output delivering 1.8 GW, representing 17.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Thanks to this abundance of clean power, Scottish carbon intensity sits at 0 gCO2/kWh, standing in stark contrast to the 176 gCO2/kWh registered GB-wide. However, grid transmission bottlenecks continue to limit cross-border transfer. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 578 MWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a constraint cost of about £38,660. Compensating for this stranded renewable electricity required an estimated 109,820 cubic meters of gas burned elsewhere on the network, which released an unnecessary 202 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Extrapolating today’s constraint expenditure yields an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £14 million. When distributed across Great Britain's typical annual demand of roughly 280 million MWh, these balancing actions add an estimated £0.05/MWh to everybody’s invoice in the UK, clearly demonstrating the financial and environmental penalties imposed by regional transmission infrastructure constraints.
